spec.idea: One 256-thread threadgroup per row with half4 vector loads/stores (overloaded for device/constant address spaces), simd_sum + tiny threadgroup reduction, and the second pass re-reading the just-written h from cache instead of holding it in registers (scalar fallback when H%4!=0).

128-thread row groups keep h and w in registers (up to 8 half4 per thread, all loads issued up front) so there is no second global re-read, with only a 4-entry threadgroup reduction; scalar fallback for H%4!=0 or H>4096.

k001's register-resident single-pass layout, with w kept as half4 to cut register pressure, a vectorized register-free tail so H>4096 no longer falls to the scalar path, and a cheaper balanced reduction.

128-thread row groups issue all x, r and w vector loads up front (w latency hidden behind the reduction), keep h in registers for the second pass, and use a 4-entry balanced reduction with a vectorized re-read tail for H>4096.

One 32-thread simdgroup per row (4 rows per threadgroup) so the reduction is a single simd_sum with no threadgroup memory or barriers, h held in registers as half4 for the second pass, and w loaded only after the reduction.

k000's 256-thread-per-row layout, but with x/r/w half4 loads all issued up front and h kept in registers (exactly 4 half4 per thread at H=4096), so the second pass has no re-read and w latency hides behind the reduction; H>4096 falls back to a re-read tail.
